text.p: Following are the main stories in Monday's Malaysian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad said the newly-formed Co-operation for Development or D-8 must show results to gain credibility.
-- The government is determined to change the "old culture" of Sabah politics, even at the risk of facing defection by its state leaders, acting Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim said.
-- As of midnight on Sunday, 91 children have been admitted at government hospitals in Peninsular Malaysia for suspected hand-foot-mouth disease, an increase of 15 from the day before.
-- Maju Holdings Sdn Bhd will go it alone in the privatisation exercise of Perwaja Steel Sdn Bhd as the Lion Group has failed to confirm its participation by the midnight deadline last Friday.
-- The Domestic Trade and Consumer Affairs Ministry has frozen the issuance of permits for cheap sales to formulate a better system to curb profiteering.

-- Bumi Armada Bhd, en route to a listing on the Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange main board, has forecast a 64 percent increase in turnover for 1997 supported by the increased provision of marine transportation and support services to the oil and gas industry.
-- The management of cash-rich fast-food chain KFC Holdings BHd was in a bit of a flap last week when institutional investors raised questions about how the group has been managing its surplus funds.

-- The much-hyped proposed merger of MBF Capital with Suria Capital Holdings is unlikely to take place. Banking sources say Bank Negara Malaysia has recommended to the Finance Ministry that permission not be granted to the two parties to proceed with merger talks.
